then.text: Off you go to Pyla. Tell Hüseyin I said he's right. Tell Andreas I said he's right. That's diplomacy.

You beat the critic? Then you're a judge worth listening to. My verdict: same cheese, two names, one island. My mother made it, your Andreas's mother made it. The EU wrote both names on one form in 2021, so it's official.
Go and tell them in Pyla. And tell them the best one is mine.

else.text: The south sent you? Good. But first, that critic by the fountain says hellim is 'squeaky rubber'. In front of my stall. Settle it, and I'll give you my verdict.
Hellim, fresh and in brine! Fry it with tomatoes, or eat it in a sandwich with a slice of watermelon in summer.

nn_weaver.text: Lefkara lace is from a village in the south, hand-stitched. My weaving is from the north. We sell at the same craft fairs and admire each other's work very loudly, so the customers hear.

nn_teacher_tr.text: Merhaba! That's hello. 'Günaydın' is good morning, 'teşekkür ederim' is thank you, and 'sağ ol' is the quick, friendly thanks.
Before a meal, say 'afiyet olsun', enjoy it. To someone at work, say 'kolay gelsin', may it come easy. There's a phrase for everything. It's a very sociable language.
Turkish letters to watch: ş is 'sh', ç is 'ch', and ı without a dot is a sound English hasn't got, somewhere between the 'a' in 'about' and a grunt.
